newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at record high.

text.p: Swiss shares rebounded from opening losses to post a third straight record close after the index rose on the back of gains in the financials sector.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed 30.4 points, or 0.54 percent, higher at 5,700.3 and the broad Swiss Performance Index was up 15.62 points, or 0.44 percent, to 3,593.51.
Bourse volume stood at 2.57 billion Swiss francs.
"The bourse favourites change by the day," one trader noted, adding that financials were favoured today while recent high-flyers such as Nestle, Novartis and Roche were neglected.

Zurich Group continued to be bolstered by news of its imminent purchase of U.S. asset manager Scudder, Stevens & Clark. The stock rose 11 francs to 600, reflecting the market's positive view of the deal.
Among banks, SBC and Credit Suisse jumped 19 francs to 395.50 and seven francs to 196.0, respectively. Dealers said the gains were the result of large buy orders.
One dealer cited old rumours the two banks may merge some back office activities.
ABB also was among the day's winners, climbing 26 francs to 2,220.
Novartis registered shares consolidated recent gains, giving up four francs to end at 2,363. Nestle fell three to 1,940.
